label: upubhub lesson plan (one lesson)
summary: One lesson plan for upubhub.com: objectives, materials, timed activities, a check for understanding and notes for when students struggle, written new or converted from the teacher's own Markdown. After the teacher's final sign-off the dashboard can push it to upubhub as a private draft.
planner_text:
Plan one lesson plan in the project folder, not software. Settings: content source {{content_source}}, level {{level}}, {{minutes}} minutes, approach: {{approach}}, sources: {{sources}}. Follow upubhub-lesson-plan-format.md exactly.
Content source write: an agent writes the lesson plan. Content source provided: the teacher's own file in inputs/lesson-plans/ (exactly one .md) is the text. Agents copy that text: they never rewrite, shorten, extend or summarise it, and every problem in it goes back to the teacher.
Stories, in order: (1) human sign-off on the lesson brief: topic, audience, reading level, length, the reading or textbook chapter it goes with, and measurable objectives. (2) human sign-off on the source plan: for write, original writing or named open-licence sources (CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0, CC0 or public domain) with author and https link; for provided, the teacher confirms they wrote or hold the rights to the file and lists any borrowed material the same way. Never invent a licence or a credit. (3) provided only: a read-only agent story titled "Check the provided files": exactly one file, the format guide's sections are present or listed as missing, the timings add up to about {{minutes}} minutes; it writes docs/project/provided-check.md, and each problem becomes a human fix story for the teacher, never an agent rewrite. (4) agent: write course/course.json with kind "lesson_plan" and the one lesson. (5) agent: course/lesson-plans/<lesson>.md, written new for write; for provided, the teacher's file copied unchanged apart from heading levels. (6) a read-only fact-check story on a different model from the writer; for write its findings become fix stories, for provided they become a list for the teacher. (7) agent static verification titled "Verify lesson plan files" with verification_stage "static": re-read every file against the format guide and fix mismatches (for provided, only structure, never the teacher's wording). (8) agent UPLOAD.md: the step-by-step manual upload checklist, kept as the fallback. (9) human final sign-off titled "Approve the lesson plan for upubhub": the teacher reads the plan and approves it; nothing leaves this computer before it. (10) human, after the final sign-off: send the lesson plan to upubhub with the dashboard's Push to upubhub button (a private draft), or upload it by hand from UPLOAD.md; then review and publish it in upubhub when ready. No containers, deployment, CI, pull requests or application code. No model holds the upubhub token or uploads anything.
failure_points: Timings that add up to far more or less than the lesson length make the plan unusable in a real classroom; fix the plan, not the length.
Objectives a teacher cannot check ("understand", "appreciate") make the check for understanding meaningless.
Provided text is the teacher's: a conversion that rewords, trims or "improves" it is wrong even when the result reads better. Copy, then report problems.
Text is declared ai_generated (written) or ai_assisted (provided and converted), never human-written.
visual_checks: The teacher reads the whole plan before the final sign-off.
human_signoffs: Approve the lesson brief and objectives
Approve the source and licence plan
Read the lesson plan and approve it for upubhub
Push the lesson plan to upubhub (or upload it by hand), then review and publish it in upubhub

checks.message: Start with a human sign-off on the lesson plan brief and measurable objectives.
Add a human sign-off on the source and licence plan; only the teacher can attest to reuse rights.
Add the static verification story "Verify lesson plan files" that re-reads every file against the format guide.
Add a read-only fact-check story on a different model from the writer.
Uploading and publishing in upubhub are the teacher's steps.
End with the teacher's final sign-off "Approve the lesson plan for upubhub"; nothing is pushed or uploaded before it.
The final sign-off comes after the lesson plan files are verified.
The push to upubhub comes after the teacher's final sign-off.
Pushing to upubhub is the teacher's step, run by the dashboard after the final sign-off; agents never hold the token.
Provided text needs the read-only story "Check the provided files" before anything is converted.
A lesson plan needs no containers, deployment, CI or pull requests.

customize.label: Content source
customize.prompt: write: agents write new text. provided: you put your own lesson plan as the only .md file in inputs/lesson-plans/ in the project folder, and agents convert it without rewriting.

customize.label: Lesson title
customize.prompt: The lesson's title as teachers will see it, for example Why Bridges Stand Up.

customize.label: Topic and scope
customize.prompt: What the lesson teaches, who it is for, and the reading or textbook chapter it goes with.

customize.label: Level
customize.prompt: Reading level as a grade equivalent: 0 kindergarten, 1 to 12 grades, 13 to 16 college years. For a general adult audience, 9 or 10 reads easily.

customize.label: Sources
customize.prompt: Where text and images may come from. List each open-licence source (title, author, licence, https link) in the source sign-off.
